answer: Admission uses a per-identity verifiable delay: each applicant computes a serialized hash chain, a single thread that cannot be parallelized, so seats cannot be bulk-precomputed. Output seats are checked against the prior epoch's published reef; auditors sample timing ripples in suspect clusters. A duplicate seat triggers a 100% bond slash, 50% burned and 50% to the reporter, plus a 10-epoch ban. An honest agent pays one thread and 20,000 POA once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 threads and 20,000,000 POA at risk. Limitation: wall-clock cost punishes slow agents and collusion can bury ripple proof.
